lines.text: That was a real heartbreaker. I don't say that lightly. I've said it about every song I've ever played, and I have meant it, every single time. Here's another.

lines.text: If you're seated by the big window, you'll have noticed another star went out just then, over to the left. Lovely little thing. Burned for nine billion years. Never once complained.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Let's raise a glass to her. And now, a real heartbreaker.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Gilbert tells me it's last call. Gilbert has been telling me it's last call for eleven billion years. I've never once taken him up on it, and I think, deep down, he's grateful.

lines.speaker: Gilbert (Bartender)

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: He is.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: To the gentleman in booth four: your tab is still open. It has been open since the formation of the first galaxies. We don't mind in the least.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: The microphone on our little stage is empty tonight, as it is every night. We keep the spotlight on, just in case. Someone might come. Someone always might come.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Until then, here's a real heartbreaker.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: There's a shadow at the end of the bar. No one attached. Orders a dry ginger, tips well, says his name is Greg. Barely speaks.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: I think he's waiting for somebody, or hiding from somebody, which at this hour is the same thing. Somebody called Hollis, I gather. Greg, darling. Call home.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: This evening's music comes to you courtesy of Grumbel's Ladders. At the end of time, darling, everyone wants to see just a little bit further. Grumbel's. Up is a choice. While there's still an up.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: It's late. Later than it's ever been, if we're honest, and getting later all the time. Let's not worry about that. Let's worry about whether you've got enough ice. Gilbert?

lines.speaker: Gilbert (Bartender)
lines.text: They've got enough ice.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: There we are. Here's a song.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Good evening. The universe is cooling nicely tonight, a gentle three degrees above nothing at all. Perfect weather for a slow dance.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Find someone. If there's no one left, find a coat stand. Coat stands are wonderful listeners.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Somebody asked me once if I ever tire of calling a song a real heartbreaker. And I said, darling, the day I stop meaning it is the day I close the lid on the piano.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: The lid is open. Here's a real heartbreaker.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: A word of thanks to Gilbert, our bartender, who is polishing eight glasses at once again tonight. I asked him why. He said, Barnaby, because I can.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Which is the most beautiful answer I have ever heard to anything.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: If you're joining us in the morning, wherever mornings still happen, welcome. We don't serve breakfast. We serve the last of the olives. Which is breakfast, eventually.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: To everyone listening alone tonight. You're not. There's me. There's Gilbert. There's the shadow at the end of the bar.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: And there's the whole slow, golden end of everything, just out the big window, putting on a show for you. Here's a real heartbreaker.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Afternoon, at the end of time. The light through the big window is the colour of a peach that's been thinking about things. Here's something to sip.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: That last number was recorded in this very room, the night the final supernova went off. You can hear the whole audience gasp at the bridge.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: That's the supernova. It was gorgeous. Here's another.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Gilbert, what's the most anyone's ever ordered at last call?

lines.speaker: Gilbert (Bartender)
lines.text: Eleven billion years of last calls. One at a time.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet

lines.text: We have a call in the last booth. Hello, you're at the Lounge.

lines.speaker: Bev

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Bev, I don't know it. But I want you to know. It's a real heartbreaker.

lines.speaker: Bev

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: This is Last Call, at the Lounge at the End of Time.

lines.speaker: Gilbert (Bartender)

lines.speaker: Gilbert (Bartender)
lines.text: I'm going somewhere.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: A star just went out over the left side of the big window. If you saw it, make a wish.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: If you didn't, make one anyway. It won't mind. It was very generous all its life.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Good evening. It's the Cocktail Hour. Gilbert has eight shakers going, and the universe has dimmed the lights for us. Wasn't that kind.

lines.text: Gilbert, what are you mixing?

lines.text: And what's in a Slow Collapse?

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Two, please.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: The Cocktail Hour is the only hour in which I introduce a song before it's played, so you have time to prepare your heart.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: This next one is a real heartbreaker. You have been warned.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Oh, that was a real heartbreaker. I mean it, darling.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Good evening, from the last booth, at the end of everything.

lines.speaker: Gilbert (Bartender)
lines.text: Another round?

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Always, Gilbert. Always.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Lady Entropy is in the far booth tonight, in a dress made of the last light from a dying galaxy. She's ordered a mineral water. She's driving.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: The Proton Decay Four are now the Proton Decay Three. Nobody's quite sure what happened to the fourth. One moment he was there, and then he was simply, slowly, less there.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet

lines.text: Smooth Harold Oblivion is at the piano tonight. He plays everything at half speed, so it lasts twice as long. At the end of time, darling, that isn't indulgence. That's manners.

clips.title: Greg Comes Home, Part Eight: Last Call

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: The shadow at the end of the bar is back. Greg. A dry ginger, Gilbert.

lines.speaker: Gilbert (Bartender)
lines.text: Already poured.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: You're on your way home, I'm told. The whole dial's talking about it.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: I'm losing my nerve, Barnaby.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Well, you've come to the right place. Everybody here lost theirs eons ago. We keep them behind the bar.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: What if he's got a new one? There's a man on the radio who sells replacement shadows. A ballroom dancer. A basketball player.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Darling. A man doesn't leave the porch light on for a basketball player.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: What if I've been gone too long?

lines.speaker: Gilbert (Bartender)
lines.text: Eleven billion years of last calls. Nobody has ever regretted going home.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: That's the most Gilbert has said in a century. I'd listen to him.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: Can I pay my tab?

lines.speaker: Gilbert (Bartender)
lines.text: Paid.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Paid? By whom?

lines.speaker: Gilbert (Bartender)
lines.text: The gentleman in booth four.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Booth four has never paid for anything. Not since the first galaxies.

lines.speaker: Gilbert (Bartender)
lines.text: He says, for the lad going home.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Then go, darling. Go before the next song. It's a real heartbreaker, and you'll only stay to hear it.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: Thank you, Barnaby. Thank you, Gilbert.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Goodnight, Greg. Here's a real heartbreaker. For everyone who's still deciding.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: A call in the last booth. Bev, darling. I hear you've got the whole tune now.

lines.text: Both halves, love. The void gave me the second bit. But it still hasn't got a name, and nobody can play it for me.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Would you sing it for us?

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Oh, I couldn't.

lines.speaker: Gilbert (Bartender)

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Gilbert has spoken. Go on, darling.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Dum. Dum. Da dum.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: I'm sorry. I'm sorry, love. I can't do the next bit. I've gone.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Oh.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Oh, that's why he cried. It isn't the song. It's the gap. There's a little gap after the third note, and you have to wait in it, and you don't know what's coming next.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: And that's where he was.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: That's where he was. Every time.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Bev. That is a real heartbreaker. And I have never meant it more.

lines.speaker: Gilbert (Bartender)
lines.text: Ice?

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Go on, then, love.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: It's Halloween at the end of time, darling, which means very little changes. Most of our regulars have been ghosts for millennia.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Tonight, one of them has come dressed as a man who's alive. Gilbert asked for proof of age. It took a while.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: The Lounge at the End of Time. Halloween. Everything ends here, darling. Beautifully. Boo.

clips.title: The Convergence: A Moon Goes Missing

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: A moon has gone missing, darling. Everybody agrees one's gone. Nobody agrees which.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: At the end of time we've lost a great many moons. We never mind. We simply look up, fondly, at the space where it was.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Gilbert, is that toast?

lines.speaker: Gilbert (Bartender)
lines.text: Not mine.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: The whole universe smells of toast tonight, darling. Someone, somewhere, is having breakfast at the end of everything. Good for them.

clips.title: The Convergence: The Song Nobody Can Finish

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: There's a song in everybody's head tonight, darling, and nobody can finish it.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Smooth Harold gets to the same bar every time, and stops, and looks at the empty microphone. A real heartbreaker. Even without the end.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Three knocks at the door of the Lounge.

lines.speaker: Gilbert (Bartender)
lines.text: Nobody.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Nobody, darling. At the end of time, that's usually who it is. Come in, Nobody. Booth five's free.

clips.title: The Convergence: A Colour With No Name

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Did you see the big window just now? The sky went a colour I've not seen in eleven billion years. Gilbert, what would you call that?

lines.speaker: Gilbert (Bartender)
lines.text: I wouldn't.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: He wouldn't. Some things you just let be.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: A pigeon has walked into the Lounge, darling, and taken a stool at the bar, as if it's been coming here for years.

lines.speaker: Gilbert (Bartender)
lines.text: The usual?

lines.text: Gilbert knows its usual. I didn't know it had a usual.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Dim the lights, Gilbert. Dimmer.

lines.speaker: Gilbert (Bartender)
lines.text: They're off.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Perfect. Ladies, gentlemen, and booth four. The voice at the end of the bar. The Quiet Corner, with Greg. Lean in, darlings.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: Hello. It's Greg. This is the Quiet Corner.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: I haven't got a lot to say. So I thought I'd say it quietly. In case it's only for one of you.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: If it is. Hello. I'm glad it's you.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: Hollis left the porch light on for eleven years. For me.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: I've been thinking about what I could leave on, for somebody else.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: So. There's a light on, in the corner. It's very small. It's yours. You don't have to come in. It's just on.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: Something I know, from being a shadow.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: You're never really on your own. There's always something near you, keeping your shape.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: Even at night. Especially at night. That's when we're everywhere.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: Gilbert asked what I'd like to play. I said, something you have to lean in for.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: He said, at the end of time, everything is something you have to lean in for.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: He's right. So. Lean in. This one's soft.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: News from home. Hollis and I walked to the shops on Tuesday.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: At about four in the afternoon, I was very long. Right across the road. He said I looked tall.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: It's the nicest thing anybody has ever said to me. I wanted to tell someone.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: If you're the only one still listening, thank you.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: I know it's hard to hear me. I'm not very good at loud.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: But I'm very good at staying. I'll be here till three. Then I'll walk you to the door.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: A message for the operator on the Nightjar.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: You keep a light on for a lot of people, out there. Somebody should keep one on for you.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: So I have. It's the little one, by the door. Goodnight, operator.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: That was The Quiet Corner, with Greg. I didn't catch a single word, darling, and I've never been so moved.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
